a39b75c013f25931d216d70e7c49d107cae90b46.summary: Project page for Sliver, an open-source, cross-platform adversary emulation and red team framework intended for authorised security testing. It describes command-and-control over mTLS, WireGuard, HTTP(S) and DNS, support for macOS, Windows and Linux, and GPLv3 licensing with install instructions. It describes a tool, not a threat actor, campaign, malware incident or vulnerability, so it is not a threat report.

a35cc21a595cd3651df0e7ad8e3f2eb726939764.summary: GitHub repository README by Tillmann Werner about the Conficker computer worm. It provides YARA rules to detect unpacked worm variants in memory, Snort rules to detect exploitation attempts in a network, and unpacked sample versions of each Conficker generation, which the README warns contain malicious code. The last commit is dated November 20, 2018, and the data is stated as copyright 2008-2018.

a32666781a0f2225f289f72a0537cc3b6a031ad9.summary: Elastic Security Labs introduces the REF5961 intrusion set, which targets governments in Southern and Southeastern Asia, including the foreign affairs ministry of an ASEAN member. It discloses three new malware families (EAGERBEE, RUDEBIRD, DOWNTOWN) and links them to the REF2924 intrusion set and to a campaign against Mongolian government-themed lures. Elastic assesses the operators as state-sponsored and China-nexus. Links to LuckyMouse and TA428 are described as alignments or attributions made by others, with hedged confidence.

hedges: Elastic says it is confident the operators are China-nexus, based on overlaps in execution flows, tooling, infrastructure and victimology.
The state-sponsored, espionage-motivated description of the REF2924 and REF5961 operators is Elastic's own assessment.
The LuckyMouse link rests on string formatting and behaviour that only aligns with earlier research.
SManager/PhantomNet has been attributed to TA428 by earlier reporting; the report only links DOWNTOWN to it with a moderate degree of confidence.
DOWNTOWN is attributed to a nationally sponsored Chinese threat actor with a moderate degree of confidence; the report has little visibility into its overall impact.
The report has a high degree of confidence that the malware and campaign operators share a tasking authority or organizational umbrella.
The report says the Mongolian government or NGOs may have been targeted by REF2924, and that it is not clear how the infrastructure was compromised or how far it was used.
The report cannot confirm that the self-signed TLS certificate was used for EAGERBEE or RUDEBIRD, although TLS to an IP address is a configuration option.
